title: US investigates whether Iran is behind cyberattacks and bomb threats against tankers, ynet reports citing WSJ
date_note: Al-Monitor and Fox News, both published 23 November, cite the Wall Street Journal report of that Monday; ynet and LSM relayed it on 24 November. Attacks cited include September ones.
geo_basis: United States, where the investigation and the Coast Guard response are reported; the ships' locations vary
summary: Ynet, Al-Monitor and LSM, relaying a Wall Street Journal report, say US officials are investigating whether Iran, or possibly Russia, is behind cyberattacks on tankers. NPR, also citing the WSJ, says an unnamed US official described attackers exploiting known vulnerabilities in Fortinet FortiGate devices; NPR says the FBI and Coast Guard reported no operational disruptions from August boardings. Baird Maritime, relaying the WSJ, says at least four more ships were boarded. Iran is not confirmed.
plain: Ynet and NPR, citing the Wall Street Journal, say US officials are investigating whether Iran is behind cyberattacks on tankers. NPR says an unnamed official described known FortiGate flaws being exploited. Iran is not confirmed.
exec: Ynet reports the US is investigating cyberattacks and bomb threats on tankers, some bound for US ports; whether Iran is behind them is not confirmed.
action: No action needed; for awareness. NPR says the Coast Guard and FBI issued a joint bulletin in September warning that attackers scan for unpatched vulnerabilities.

evidence.quote: The offshore operations took place Aug. 21 and 24 in the Gulf of America
Threat actors routinely scan for specific, unpatched vulnerabilities to gain a foothold.

validation.note: Two publishers read (ynet, Hebrew; Al-Monitor relaying Reuters), both relaying one Wall Street Journal report that was not read, so the core fact is single-origin. Al-Monitor says Reuters could not immediately verify the report. Fox News (read) quotes a Coast Guard spokesperson confirming the boardings; its account of the attacks also relays the Wall Street Journal. LSM (24 Nov) also relays the WSJ report (up to 50 ships; Russia not ruled out); it is the same single origin. NPR (read via OPB, 24 Nov) also relays the WSJ report with an unnamed US official as source; same single origin. Baird Maritime (25 Nov, read) also relays the WSJ, adding at least four more boarded ships; same single origin.

review.note: stronger than the source: removed main suspect from exec; told NPR changed to NPR says agencies reported no disruptions from August boardings
